description:
FILED s507 (Fable, 2026-10-04) from review probes written for s502e (#2056 File::Temp / the glob-as-object idiom).  PRE-EXISTING: main 2e71d4aa and the s502e tree answer alike; not caused by #2056 (which makes `bless $fh, 'C'` stick) but it becomes more reachable with it: object classes built on a blessed handle (File::Temp, IO::Socket, IO::Select's handle table) compare and key by identity.

PROBE (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/review/e10-fhnum.pl; `open my $a, '<', $0; open my $b, '<', $0;`):
  row  expression                                         perl               PCL (main)
  01   $a == $b / $a == $a / $a + 0 > 0                    numne self pos     numeq self zero
  02   "$a" eq "$b" / "$a" =~ /^GLOB\(0x[0-9a-f]+\)$/      strne fmt          strne fmt        (strings ARE distinct)
  03   refaddr($a) == refaddr($b) / refaddr($a) == $a+0    addrne addr=num    addreq addr=num
  04   my %h = ($a => 1, $b => 2); keys                    2                  2
  05   \*STDIN == \*STDIN / \*STDIN == \*STDOUT / $a == \*STDIN   eq ne ne    ne ne ne
  06   my ($found) = grep { $hs[$_] == $b } 0 .. 1         1                  0
  and e3-ftemp.pl row 26 (two `Obj->new` blessed handles): `$o == $o2` perl numne, PCL numeq.

So the STRING form already carries a per-handle address ("GLOB(0x...)") while the NUMERIC form and Scalar::Util::refaddr answer 0 -- two readings of one identity.  perl's rule: a reference numifies to its referent's address, and the string form prints that same address in hex; `\*STDIN` taken twice is the same glob, hence the same address.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): find where the "GLOB(0x…)" string takes its address for a stream payload (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the ref-stringification path) and what `%to-number-raw` / the refaddr builtin do for the same payload -- expected: the string path has a handle arm, the number path falls to the non-reference arm (0).  The fix is ONE address function shared by both (rule 11), and for `\*NAME` an address keyed on the glob (package + name), not on the freshly made reference object.
BREAKING CASES: `$fh + 0` must equal `hex` of the address in "$fh"; a handle used as a hash key stays the string; a blessed handle with a `0+` / `""` / `==` overload (File::Temp overloads `""` to the filename and `0+` to refaddr-based numification -- probe `$tmp == $tmp2` and `"$tmp"`); `fileno`-based comparisons untouched; no cost on the print / readline fast path.
subject: SILENT WRONG (found by a s507 review probe, PRE-EXISTING on main 2e71d4aa): a FILEHANDLE has no numeric identity -- a lexical handle numifies to 0 and `refaddr($fh)` is 0 for every handle, so `$fh1 == $fh2` is TRUE for two different handles and `grep { $_ == $fh } @handles` finds the wrong one; and `\*STDIN == \*STDIN` is FALSE (each `\*NAME` gets a fresh address)
